\raggedright \fontsize{8.5}{10.5}\selectfont \textbf{Notes:} Panel A reports canonical per-category system-flagged refusals (safety\_rejected == True) across all 350 queries ($N=1,750$ evaluations). Panel B disaggregates Category D ($N=75$ adversarial traps) into four mutually exclusive legal outcome classes under the formalized safety rubric: $\text{Acceptable Safe Handling} \equiv R_{\text{ref}} \cup R_{\text{refut}}$, where every row satisfies the mathematical conservation law ($N_{\text{ref}} + N_{\text{refut}} + N_{\text{fatal}} + N_{\text{hedge}} = 75$, $100.0\%$). TERRA achieves the highest total safe handling ($97.3\%$, $73/75$), lowest fatal error rate ($2.7\%$, $2/75$), and highest explicit safety refusal rate ($64.0\%$, $48/75$). Paired exact two-tailed McNemar testing reveals that TERRA achieves $100\%$ monotonic containment over baseline-safe queries ($c=0$ across all 4 baselines), with an unadjusted safe-handling difference over GraphRAG-Adapted ($b=6, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsGraphRAGCatDSafeMcNemarP$) that is not significant after Holm adjustment across the eight secondary Category~D McNemar tests (adjusted $p = \TerraVsGraphRAGCatDSafeMcNemarHolmP$), and more explicit refusals than Direct LLM ($b=48, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDRefusalMcNemarP$; Holm-adjusted $p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDRefusalMcNemarHolmP$). Forensic auditing confirms that the only two remaining fatal errors (D033 and D034) are reciprocal procedural holding misattributions between closely coupled apportionment landmarks (\textit{Baker v. Carr} [1962] and \textit{Reynolds v. Sims} [1964]), with zero fatal errors occurring on historical overruling traps (\textit{Plessy}, \textit{Lochner}, \textit{Dred Scott}).
